name: ema_crossover_5s
author: adapted from AI_Quant
thesis: This strategy captures short-term trend flips: when EMA9 crosses EMA21, it signals a momentum shift. Many traders focus on longer signals, so a quick cross can indicate a new trend phase. It exploits that older traders lag behind short-term moves. It persists due to continual market noise and the constant emergence of new trader participation.
mechanism: Moving average crossovers detect shifts in the balance between recent and historical average prices. A bullish crossover indicates that recent institutional buying has pushed the short-term average above the long-term, reflecting a change in the dominant order flow direction. The new trend persists as algorithms and discretionary traders align with the crossover signal.
weaknesses: Small targets (0.5%) give tight edge which may be eroded by costs
Relies on moving averages that lag during sudden moves
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
